newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares mixed, seen up on Friday.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares mixed, seen up on Friday.

text.p: Polish shares were mixed after a three-session fall and analysts said the market, pushed up 0.6 percent on Thursday by large-cap rises, should extend gains on Friday and continue its three-month horizontal trend.
Analysts said May earnings data released this week were mediocre but that optimism over Wednesday's news that large Bank Handlowy's privatisation offer was heavily oversubscribed cheered the market.
"The oversubscription is a good sign, it shows interest in big Polish firms, seen by today's outperformance by the WIG 20 (large cap index)," said Bogdan Kornacki of WBK brokerage.
The retail tranche of Poland's largest commercial bank was three times subscribed and the institutional tranche 17.4 times subscribed with foreign demand exceeding $3.5 billion.

The main market's all-share WIG index rose 0.6 percent to 15,996.9 points and turnover rose 17.6 percent to 137.6 million zlotys ($42.4 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 53 to 38 with 15 stocks flat.

Analysts said much of the money mobilised in the Handlowy oversubscription could go to the public offering of copper giant KGHM Polska Miedz SA starting in late June, though enough should go to stocks to prevent steep falls by the main index.
Computer maker Optimus jumped 7.4 percent after lifting May earnings results by about six times, analysts said.
They said the only main market stock to outperform Optimus on Thursday, paintmaker Polifarb Cieszyn, was likely helped by a higher May net this year. The stock rose 9.4 percent.

The National Investment Fund NIF index fell 2.2 percent to 151.2 points and NFI units fell 2.6 percent to 148 zlotys ($45.6) but analysts saw a possible rise by both on Friday after this week's slump.
